rule_directive: Classify an asset as 'Chain of Ruin: Technological Acceleration of Knowledge System Collapse' when it provides evidence of a three-stage pattern of epistemic collapse: 1. Pre-existing Decay: The asset documents a system (e.g., a profession, an institution) where foundational standards of diligence, verification, or knowledge integrity were already eroding due to decisions made alongside chronic, systemic pressures. 2. Technological Catalyst: A new technology is introduced into this compromised environment. The technology does not cause the decay but acts as a powerful accelerant or catalyst, making the consequences of the pre-existing negligence more severe, scalable, or visible. 3. Proactive Negligence: The core failure highlighted is the intentional choice by credentialed actors to abandon their timeless professional duties of verification. They devalue ground truth as a concept and destroy the knowledge system with this disregard, demonstrating a proactive negligence that prioritizes nihilism over integrity. In the legal system, this causes deep, irreparable structural harm by permanently poisoning official court records with citations to nonexistent cases and phantom precedents—severing the foundational epistemic lineage where judicial records must reliably point to real, verifiable precedent.

rule_directive: Classify an asset as 'Paradigm-Constrained Remediation' when it documents a scenario where practitioners from a structurally flawed professional paradigm attempt to solve a crisis that their own paradigm created or exacerbated.
